evidence: Draft: 'Each route below was given frozen criteria committed before its scripts'. TEN_DOORS_RESULT:29: 'Doors 5 and 8: the frozen question preceded the scripts by file times but was not committed first.' CFG131 README:3: the frozen question was 'NOT committed, per the run's instruction'. Git history at 53f374ae2: for 5 of the 25 rows the frozen file and the first script were added in the same commit (door 5 CFG130 c1d719fbf; door 8 CFG131 aa0d95aef; 11A CFG171 1c91164e9; 11D CFG251 eff33f041; CFG253 c89139c1b); the other 20 have the frozen file in an earlier commit. For all five the lanes record that the criteria were written before any script (file times, or a sha256 recorded before the script existed for CFG251 and CFG253), so no verdict depends on this; the sentence as written is false, and it is the draft's statement of its preregistration discipline.
independent_support: an explicit source statement (TEN_DOORS_RESULT:29) plus an independent git-history recomputation (CFG265_route_recount.py)
proposed_fix: 'Each route below has frozen criteria written before its scripts: for 20 of the 25 they were committed in an earlier commit; for doors 5, 8, 11A, 11D and CFG253 they were written first (by file time, or with a recorded hash) and committed together with the scripts, as TEN_DOORS_RESULT and those lanes disclose.'

evidence: 'The bare law's floor is 1.161 (alt 1.192)' is Arm A, the merged law with the nu_RAR kernel (DOOR11_RESULT:36: Arm A's band 'uses the nu_RAR kernel ... not P2'); the same paragraph then gives the P2-kernel merge, 1.063-1.127, without saying the two are different kernels of the same bare law. 'gamma <= 1.077 kills the bare law' is Arm A's floor minus 3 x 0.028 (CFG63's 'frozen-rounded' value); the preregistration falsifies Arm A only below 1.056 and reads 1.056-1.084 as 'disfavored (2.8-3.8 sigma_tot)'; and 1.077 is the TOP of the P2 merge at the variant field (DOOR11_RESULT:37), so for the P2 law it is not a kill line. 'cap 8.1 sigma' and '3 sigma needs about 4,300 pairs' are Arm A numbers; for the P2 merge CFG200 gives 2.3-3.7 sigma at N = 30,000 and 14,000-264,000 pairs for 3 sigma, and no separation from the derivation chain's ceiling (0.2-1.1 sigma, never 3). 'gamma >= 1.084 kills B' holds only if the frozen stability checks pass (and gamma < 1.23). A reader concludes that DR4 separates B from 'the bare law' at 5.8 sigma with about 4,300 pairs; with the programme's primary P2 kernel it is 2.3-3.7 sigma and nothing against the chain's law.
independent_support: DOOR11_RESULT Addendum 2 and CFG200 README (two source files) plus the edge table / preregistration and the P7 recomputation
proposed_fix: 'Gaia DR4 wide binaries, 2 December 2026. B predicts gamma = 1.000. Arm A, the merged law with the nu_RAR kernel, has its floor at 1.161 (alt 1.192): with the frozen sigma_sys = 0.02 its cap is 8.1 sigma and 3 sigma needs about 4,300 pairs of the ~30,000 expected; the preregistration falsifies Arm A below 1.056 and reads 1.056-1.084 as disfavored. With the P2 kernel the merged law gives 1.063-1.102 (canonical; 1.079-1.127 alt), 2.3-3.7 sigma from ownership at N = 30,000 (canonical), and it cannot be separated from the derivation chain's ceiling (0.2-1.1 sigma). gamma >= 1.084 kills B if the frozen stability checks pass. B, LCDM and Newton all predict 1.000, so for B this is a survival test, never a confirmation.' Abstract (vii): '... a survival test of B against the merged (no-ownership) law: decisive against Arm A's nu_RAR kernel, 2.3-3.7 sigma against the P2 kernel.'

evidence: Title 'What a Complete Mechanism ... Must Do'; abstract (iv) 'The failures sharpen the target into a specification'; line 155 'the target is ...'. The sources label the core of S1-S3 a reading: TEN_DOORS_RESULT:23 'Cross-door pattern (a READING, not a theorem) ... One reading: the missing object must itself carry an acceleration scale'; STANDING:284 'The common thread across the doors (a reading, not a theorem): ownership must remember boundness'; STANDING:294 (CFG243) 'Reading: the mechanism needs (1) an early cold fluid ... (2) a separate, perfectly remembering ownership assignment'; CFG242 README:3 'nothing is a theorem'; CFG230 states its requirements 'inside the stated hypotheses' of the scored classes. The draft itself labels the same content 'a reading and not a theorem' at line 136, then promotes it to what a mechanism 'must do' in the title, abstract and one-sentence summary. Only S3's 'an acceleration scale must enter' (dimension theorem, monomials) and S1's 'cosmic amount at recombination' (the inherited CMB gate) rest on more than the failure of one to three scored classes each.
independent_support: two source lines (TEN_DOORS_RESULT:23, STANDING:284) plus the draft's own line 136
proposed_fix: Abstract (iv): 'The failures suggest a specification (a reading of the scored classes, not a theorem; only the acceleration-scale item rests on a theorem, for monomials): ...'. Section 4 opener: 'Each item is a reading of the failures of scored classes: a necessary condition only inside those classes' hypotheses (CFG230). S3's acceleration scale is the one theorem-backed item; S1's cosmic amount is the inherited CMB gate.' Line 155: 'In one sentence, the reading is: ...'. Title: either 'What the Scored Routes Suggest a Complete Mechanism Must Do' or keep it and say 'suggest' in the abstract's first use.

evidence: 'The flat law against a0 prop H(z) is limited by the baryon calibration, not by sample size [P38].' CFG241 F-01 (MAJOR) found PAPER38 v1.1's 'the limit that does not shrink with sample size is the absolute calibration ... and it is the binding one' true only as N -> infinity, with the KiDS split, the class-S compilation and the class-M galaxies currently limited by statistics or the Newtonian regime. F-01'). The draft restates the corrected gloss and attributes it to the version that withdrew it. Graded MAJOR, not CRITICAL, by the tie rule: the correction rescoped a sentence; it did not retract a number.
independent_support: CFG241 README F-01 and PAPER38 v1.2 lines 33 and 204 (two source files)
proposed_fix: 'The flat law against a0 prop H(z): the limit that survives an unlimited sample is the absolute baryon calibration; at present sizes several lanes are also limited by statistical power or by the Newtonian regime [P38].'

evidence: 'A merged P2 law gives 1.063-1.127, which separates from ownership by 2.3-3.7 sigma': 2.3-3.7 sigma is the canonical footing (1.063-1.102); the band's alt top 1.127 is 4.60 sigma (CFG200 alt 2.86-4.60). evidence: The status page gives G_BBN/G0 = 0.98 +- 0.06 'at 95.4% for BBN ONLY'; the draft drops the confidence level. Read as 1 sigma, R < 0.824 is only 2.6 sigma away and 'excluded' would not follow; at 95.4% it is about 5 sigma. The transfer assumptions are not named: constant couplings through BBN, standard radiation and rates, negligible clock stress, the local Newton calibration; the status page adds that evolving couplings and extra radiation are untested.
proposed_fix: '... while BBN alone gives G_BBN/G0 = 0.98 +- 0.06 at 95.4% [A20, eq. 9]: that branch is excluded under its transfer assumptions (constant couplings through BBN, standard radiation and rates, negligible clock stress, the local Newton calibration); evolving couplings and extra radiation are untested, and C > 1198 follows at R >= 0.92 ...'

evidence: Fairness to MOND. Relative to the free best fit the committed likelihood gives Delta chi2 = 5.34 for Milgrom's cH0/2pi on its own footing, 7.04 for the framework's alt footing and 63.90 for its canonical footing (clustered 0.53 / 0.60 / 1.82 sigma). 'Fits SPARC as well as the framework (5.34 against 7.04 alt)' compares only with the alt footing; Milgrom's value fits at least as well as either framework footing and clearly better than the canonical one the draft calls canonical.
proposed_fix: Abstract: '... and Milgrom's cH0/2pi footing fits SPARC at least as well as either framework footing.' Section 6: '... fits SPARC at least as well as the framework (Delta chi2 5.34, against 7.04 alt and 63.9 canonical, relative to the free best fit), and kappa = 1/2 beats 1/2pi only on the rho_Lambda footing.'

evidence: Footing.lean writes Milgrom's a0 = cH/(2pi) as kappa c sqrt(G rho) with rho = 3H^2/(8 pi G), the critical (total) density. The draft defines the law with rho_Lambda throughout; in that convention Milgrom's value is sqrt(2/(3 pi Omega_Lambda)) = 0.557 at Omega_Lambda = 0.6847, not 0.461. The draft writes 'rho' without saying which.
proposed_fix: 'Written as kappa c sqrt(G rho) with rho = 3H0^2/(8 pi G), the critical density, Milgrom's value is kappa = sqrt(2/(3 pi)) = 0.461 (Lean, Footing); with rho = rho_Lambda it is about 0.56.'

evidence: ownership_not_field_local quantifies over F : R -> R -> R of the internal Newtonian field and the external field at a point (no gradients, tidal tensor or potential), with the postulated two-branch rule and a hierarchy containing a top-level and an owned system as premises; it is close to definitional (the README calls the sibling owned_boost_one 'near-definitional' and the rule a POSTULATE). The abstract's 'certifies ... that ownership is not a function of local field data' and S2's use of it as support for a requirement drop that; the abstract's dimension statement drops 'monomials' (Section 2 keeps it).
proposed_fix: Abstract (ii): '... certifies, from stated premises, that the postulated ownership rule is not a function of the internal and external field at a point, that ..., that among monomials a length prop M^(1/2) needs an acceleration scale, ...'. S2: 'Ownership is not field-local (Lean: a consequence of the postulated rule, Section 2).'

evidence: Fairness to named authors and literature scope.
